Categories.value: Giacomo Casanova|Francesco Casanova|Lotteries|Self-published work|2016 in Budapest|Files with coordinates missing SDC location of creation|Photos by Elekes Andor|Fehér kereszt fogadó (Budapest, Batthyány tér 4)

ImageDescription.value: Casanova Mansion on Batthyány square, Viziváros, Budapest, Central Europe. Around 1770 two houses – the house where Casanova stayed formerly and the house to the north of it were united in one rococo style house.  German theatre, then hungarian theatre as Falk theatre. In 1752 Casanova and his brother Francesco moved from Paris to Dresden, where his mother and sister Maria Maddalena were living. His new play, La Moluccheide, now lost, was performed at the Royal Theatre, where his mother often played in lead roles. He then visited Prague and Vienna, where the tighter moral atmosphere of the latter city was not to his liking.  Giacomo Casanova stayed here in 1757 while visiting the bathes of Buda and working on the lottery games in the Hungarian Kingdom. Location: 14128 hrsz, Batthyány Lajos tér 4 szám – Gyorskocsi utca 3 szám. Earlier: 1886, Bomben Platz in German (Bomba tér in Hungarian) Tags: Giacomo Casanova  baron Desforges Buda

Originally built 1912, designed by E. Montague Thomas to hold the Imperial Legislative Council and subsequently the Central Legislative Assembly (after 1919), till the newly constructed Parliament House of India in New Delhi (Sansad Bhawan)was inaugurated on 18 January 1927.[4]

The building also housed in the Secretariat of the Government of India, and was build after the capital of India shifted to Delhi from Calcutta, the temporary secretariat building was constructed in a few months' time in 1912, it functioned as the Secretariat for another decade, before the offices shifted to the present Secretariat Building on Raisina Hill.
